title: The lake and the self
hook: you can't see the bottom of a lake while the wind is blowing
carry: still the waves, and the self shows

segments.voice: Yesterday, Raja Yoga's monkey: restless, drunk on desire, stung by jealousy, possessed by pride. Your line: you are the watcher, not the monkey.

Stand at the edge of a lake on a windy afternoon. The surface is all chop and glitter. Somewhere down there are stones, weeds, maybe a lost key, but you can't see any of it. Come back at dawn, when the air is still. The same water. Now you can count the pebbles. Nothing was added to the lake overnight. Something was taken away. Vivekananda uses that lake to explain one short line near the start of the Yoga Sutras.
screen: `A LAKE ON A WINDY DAY.` → `THE SAME LAKE AT DAWN.` → `NOTHING ADDED. SOMETHING STILLED.`

segments.voice: Raja Yoga carries, in its second half, Vivekananda's rendering of the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali, short lines with his explanation under each. Near the very start is the line that says what yoga is. Put plainly: yoga is the stilling of the waves of the mind. The Sanskrit word for the mind-stuff is chitta. The word for its waves is vritti. And Vivekananda reaches for a lake. The bottom of the lake, he says, is our own true self. The lake is the chitta, and the waves are the vrittis. While the surface is rippled, or the water muddy, we can't see the bottom. Only when the water is clear and the waves die down do we see what was there the whole time. In the Hindu words this path has met, that bottom is the atman, the true self. That changes the goal. Nobody has to build a self, or earn one. In this picture it's already there, and the work is to let the surface settle. This is what yoga means in its home tradition. Posture matters, but in Patanjali it's one step, a steady seat for the mind's work. The stretch class is a doorway. The goal is the still lake. Vivekananda doesn't pretend it's quick. The waves keep rising: a craving, an insult remembered, a plan for tomorrow. Each time one settles, the water is a little clearer.
screen: `YOGA STILLS THE WAVES OF THE MIND.` · `THE LAKE IS CHITTA. THE WAVES ARE VRITTIS.` · `THE BOTTOM IS THE ATMAN, THE TRUE SELF.` · then, large: `NOTHING ADDED. SOMETHING STILLED.`

segments.voice: Picture a lake, any lake, under a little wind, and each time a thought rises, see it as a wave on that surface. Don't push the wave flat; let it be a wave and watch it pass back into the water, big ones and small ones, and between them, for a moment, the surface may go still. If you pray, you can rest in that stillness as your prayer.
Raja Yoga. Vivekananda's yoga of the mind, which he explains with a lake: still the waves, and the bottom, the true self, was there all along.
Your line: still the waves, and the self shows. Nothing is added to the lake, only something stilled. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: People who follow Vivekananda's teaching read Patanjali's Yoga Sutras with his explanations and keep a daily sit aimed at quieting the mind; the Ramakrishna Mission and Vedanta Societies hold classes on the text.

fork.setup: a friend says yoga is about becoming a brand-new, improved you. by Vivekananda's lake, what does Patanjali's yoga say?
options: right: it builds a better self from scratch.
it stills the mind so the self already there can be seen.

fork.reveal: in Vivekananda's picture the bottom, the true self, was there all along. yoga takes nothing away from it and adds nothing to it; it lets the waves settle.
